group.passage:
For much of the past century, many cities were planned around the car, with homes in one area, offices in another, and shopping centers on the edge of town. In such places, daily life often means long drives, and business districts that are crowded by day go [[1]] at night once the workers head home. The "fifteen-minute city," an idea made popular by Carlos Moreno, a professor in Paris, offers a different picture: a city in which most of what people need each day lies within easy [[2]] on foot or by bike.
In practice, this means building neighborhoods [[3]] enough that homes sit within a short walk of shops, schools, clinics, and parks. Paris, whose mayor made the idea a centerpiece of her re-election campaign, has added bike lanes, closed some streets outside schools to cars, and opened schoolyards to the public on weekends, letting them [[4]] as neighborhood parks. The goal is to [[5]] the hours people lose to travel, giving them more time for family, friends, and rest.
Supporters say the benefits go beyond saving time. Fewer car trips mean cleaner air and quieter streets. Small shops, cafes, and libraries help [[6]] a neighborhood, holding it together and giving it a center. A weekly market can even become a [[7]] for people from nearby areas, drawing crowds that keep local businesses going. The chance meetings that such places create matter most for older people living alone, who might otherwise feel [[8]] from the life around them.
The idea has its critics, however. In suburbs built around highways and shopping malls, homes and services are spread so far apart that the model would require costly changes. Others worry that once a neighborhood becomes pleasant to live in, rents will rise, and the very residents the plan was meant to help may be [[9]] of their own streets. Even supporters admit that the idea is no [[10]] for every urban problem, but they argue that a city designed around people rather than cars is worth working toward.

1.explanation_zh: dead 用在地方時指「死氣沉沉、冷清無人」，go dead 是「變得冷清」。白天擠滿人（crowded by day），晚上上班族一回家（once the workers head home）就變得冷清，前後形成對比。
evidence: In such places, daily life often means long drives, and business districts that are crowded by day go [[1]] at night once the workers head home.

option_notes_zh.G: isolated 是形容詞，但英文不說 go isolated，而且「孤立」講的是和外界隔絕，不是晚上沒人；isolated 屬於第 8 格。
option_notes_zh.H: double 在本文作動詞（兼作）；當形容詞「雙倍的」時，go double 也不通。
option_notes_zh.I: priced out 是片語動詞的過去分詞，go priced out 不合語法。
option_notes_zh.J: anchor（原形動詞，錨（名詞）；穩住、作為…的支柱）不合：空格在連綴動詞 go 之後，需要形容詞。

1.strategy_zh: go ___ 的 go 是連綴動詞，接形容詞；by day 和 at night 對比：白天擁擠、晚上「冷清」。
hints: go 在這裡是「變得」，後面接形容詞。

evidence: a city in which most of what people need each day lies within easy [[2]] on foot or by bike.
homes sit within a short walk of shops, schools, clinics, and parks

option_notes_zh.A: cure 是名詞，但 within easy cure 不通；cure 屬於第 10 格（no cure for）。

option_notes_zh.G: isolated（形容詞，孤立的、與外界隔絕的）不合：空格在 within easy 之後，需要名詞。

option_notes_zh.B: reach 在本文是名詞；當動詞「到達」時，reach as 也不成搭配。

option_notes_zh.E: magnet（名詞，磁鐵；吸引人的地方）不合：空格在 letting them 之後，需要原形動詞（let + O + V），並能搭配 as。
option_notes_zh.F: dead（形容詞，死的；死氣沉沉、冷清的）不合：空格在 letting them 之後，需要原形動詞（let + O + V），並能搭配 as。

option_notes_zh.F: dead（形容詞，死的；死氣沉沉、冷清的）不合：空格在 The goal is to 之後，需要原形及物動詞，受詞是 the hours people lose to travel。

option_notes_zh.H: double 也是原形及物動詞，「把耗在交通的時間加倍」只看前半句文法上可以，但後面說要讓人有更多時間給家人朋友，方向完全相反；double 屬於第 4 格（double as）。

option_notes_zh.G: isolated（形容詞，孤立的、與外界隔絕的）不合：空格在 help 之後，需要原形及物動詞（help + V），受詞是 a neighborhood。

translation_zh.text:
在過去一個世紀的大部分時間裡，許多城市都是以汽車為中心來規劃的：住家在一區、辦公室在另一區，購物中心則在城市邊緣。在這樣的地方，日常生活往往意味著長時間開車，而白天擠滿人的商業區，到了晚上上班族一回家就變得冷冷清清。由巴黎的一位教授卡洛斯．莫雷諾（Carlos Moreno）推廣的「十五分鐘城市」，描繪了一幅不同的景象：在這樣的城市裡，人們每天需要的大多數東西，走路或騎腳踏車就能輕鬆到達。
實際上，這意味著把社區建得夠緊湊，讓住家離商店、學校、診所和公園都只要走一小段路。巴黎市長把這個構想當作她競選連任的核心政見；巴黎增加了自行車道，把一些學校外面的街道改成禁止汽車通行，並在週末把校園開放給大眾，讓校園兼作社區公園。目標是縮短人們耗在交通上的時間，讓他們有更多時間陪伴家人、朋友和休息。
支持者說，好處不只是節省時間。開車的次數減少，代表空氣更乾淨、街道更安靜。小商店、咖啡館和圖書館幫忙穩住一個社區，讓它凝聚在一起，也給了它一個中心。每週一次的市集甚至可能成為吸引附近地區居民的磁鐵，帶來人潮，讓當地商家繼續經營下去。這些地方創造的偶遇，對獨居的長者最重要，否則他們可能會覺得自己和周遭的生活隔絕。
不過，這個構想也有批評者。在圍繞著高速公路和購物中心建造的郊區，住家和各種服務設施相距太遠，這個模式需要代價高昂的改變。也有人擔心，一旦社區變得宜居，房租就會上漲，而這個計畫原本想幫助的居民，反而可能因為負擔不起而被擠出自己的街區。就連支持者也承認，這個構想不是解決所有都市問題的萬靈丹，但他們認為，一座以人而不是以汽車為中心來設計的城市，值得努力去實現。
